# Tools

A skill is a tool the agent can call: one folder under [`core/tools/`](../../core/tools), holding the function and the README that documents it. The loader finds them by folder; nothing is registered by hand. To add one, see [CONTRIBUTING](../../CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [template](../../core/tools/_template/README.md).

Each name links to its README, which has the parameters, what comes back and examples.

## Offered to the agent

On Linux and macOS 6 of these 20 are left to the shell, which does the same job in one call: they are marked *Windows only*.

| Skill | What it does | Call | Offered |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`append_file`](../../core/tools/append_file/README.md) | Append text to the end of an existing file: how the next section of a large file is added, or anything that goes at its end. Deterministic; it takes no `overwrite`. | `append_file(path, content, encoding='utf-8', ensure_newline=True)` | everywhere |
| [`apply_patch`](../../core/tools/apply_patch/README.md) | Apply a unified diff — several hunks, across several files, in one call. | `apply_patch(diff='', cwd='', dry_run=False)` | everywhere |
| [`ask_user`](../../core/tools/ask_user/README.md) | Ask the user a question. In a live conversation, you ask by ending the turn. | `ask_user(topic='', context='', mode='input', prompt='', question='')` | everywhere |
| [`execute_command`](../../core/tools/execute_command/README.md) | Run a shell command and return its stdout, stderr and exit code. Each call is a new process: pass `cwd`, since `cd` does not carry over. Nothing can be typed at it: a program waiting for input meets the end of it at once. Anything meant to keep running - a server, a watcher - goes with `background=true`, or it ends only at the timeout. | `execute_command(command, cwd='', timeout=60, capture_stderr=True, max_output_chars=10000, background=False, stop_event=None)` | everywhere |
| [`file_outline`](../../core/tools/file_outline/README.md) | A file's map without its content: size, line count, top-level symbols and headings with their line numbers, and its last lines. Run it before reading a file you have not seen: it costs a fraction of the context and tells you which part to read, or where to anchor a change. | `file_outline(path, tail_lines=5, encoding='utf-8')` | everywhere |
| [`git_diff`](../../core/tools/git_diff/README.md) | Show what actually changed in the working tree, as a unified diff. | `git_diff(path='.', staged=False, file='', context_lines=3, max_chars=0)` | Windows only |
| [`git_status`](../../core/tools/git_status/README.md) | Show the state of the git repository: current branch, position relative to upstream, and which files are staged, modified or untracked, plus the last few commits. | `git_status(path='.', max_files=60)` | Windows only |
| [`glob_match`](../../core/tools/glob_match/README.md) | Find files matching a glob pattern, relative to a base directory. | `glob_match(pattern, base_path='.', max_results=0, include_ignored=False)` | Windows only |
| [`grep_search`](../../core/tools/grep_search/README.md) | Search for a regex pattern inside file contents, returning matching lines with file path and line number. | `grep_search(pattern, path='.', file_glob='*', ignore_case=False, max_results=100)` | Windows only |
| [`insert_after`](../../core/tools/insert_after/README.md) | Insert a block right after the first occurrence of an exact anchor string in a file: to add at a known place without rewriting the file. Deterministic; it takes no `overwrite`. | `insert_after(path, anchor, content, encoding='utf-8')` | everywhere |
| [`insert_before`](../../core/tools/insert_before/README.md) | Insert a block right before the first occurrence of an exact anchor string in a file: to add at a known place without rewriting the file. Deterministic; it takes no `overwrite`. | `insert_before(path, anchor, content, encoding='utf-8')` | everywhere |
| [`list_dir`](../../core/tools/list_dir/README.md) | List the contents of a directory with type, size, and modification time. | `list_dir(path='.', show_hidden=False, max_entries=200)` | Windows only |
| [`read_file`](../../core/tools/read_file/README.md) | Read the contents of a local file, optionally selecting a line range. | `read_file(path, encoding='utf-8', start_line=0, end_line=0, max_chars=0)` | Windows only |
| [`replace_in_file`](../../core/tools/replace_in_file/README.md) | Replace an exact substring in a file (`old` must appear verbatim; `count=-1` for every occurrence): the cheapest way to change part of a file you have seen. Deterministic; it takes no `overwrite`. | `replace_in_file(path, old, new, count=1, encoding='utf-8')` | everywhere |
| [`replace_in_files`](../../core/tools/replace_in_files/README.md) | Deterministic find-and-replace across many files at once — the multi-file counterpart of `replace_in_file`. Renaming a symbol project-wide costs one call instead of one per file. | `replace_in_files(old, new, path='.', file_glob='*', dry_run=False, max_files=0, encoding='utf-8')` | everywhere |
| [`revert`](../../core/tools/revert/README.md) | Undo file edits made during this session. | `revert(path='', list_only=False)` | everywhere |
| [`vision_interpret`](../../core/tools/vision_interpret/README.md) | Send a local image to a vision-capable LLM and return its textual interpretation. | `vision_interpret(image_path, question, model='', detail='auto')` | everywhere |
| [`web_fetch`](../../core/tools/web_fetch/README.md) | Perform an HTTP GET request and return the response body as text. | `web_fetch(url, timeout=30, max_chars=50000)` | everywhere |
| [`web_search`](../../core/tools/web_search/README.md) | Query DuckDuckGo and return ranked snippets with URLs. | `web_search(query, num_results=10)` | everywhere |
| [`write_file`](../../core/tools/write_file/README.md) | Create a NEW file. It refuses an existing one unless `overwrite=true`, which is for a small file regenerated whole and nothing else: change an existing file with replace_in_file, insert_after, insert_before, append_file or apply_patch. Build a large new file (a long list, a page with data, many functions) in parts: the scaffolding here, then one append_file per section; content over the size limit is refused with an error that says so. | `write_file(path, content, encoding='utf-8', create_parents=True, overwrite=False)` | everywhere |

## Used by the harness, never offered

The memory is read and written by Pragma around a turn, not by the agent inside one. These live beside the skills because they are loaded the same way.

| Skill | What it does | Call |
|---|---|---|
| [`episode_consolidate`](../../core/tools/episode_consolidate/README.md) | Consolidate a finished session transcript into a structured episodic memory record; when similar past episodes exist, also distill semantic assertions (with sources and confidence). | `episode_consolidate(transcript='', workspace='', source='', store_dir='', session_id='')` |
| [`recall_episodes`](../../core/tools/recall_episodes/README.md) | Retrieve the most relevant episodes from the episodic memory store — keyword overlap plus a same-workspace boost, no LLM call. | `recall_episodes(query='', workspace='', top_k=0, store_dir='')` |
| [`recall_learnings`](../../core/tools/recall_learnings/README.md) | Retrieve the most relevant entries from the cross-thread learnings store. Pure keyword overlap, no LLM call. | `recall_learnings(query='', top_k=0, store_path='', kinds='')` |
| [`session_reflect`](../../core/tools/session_reflect/README.md) | Reflective pass over a completed task — extracts durable, generalizable learnings and appends them to a cross-thread learnings store. | `session_reflect(transcript='', store_path='', label='')` |

## In the tree and not loaded

A folder whose name starts with an underscore is skipped by the loader.

- [`_legacy/`](../../core/tools/_legacy/README.md), retired: `call_agent`, `code`, `context_compress`, `edit_file`, `llm_invoke`, `log_event`, `parse_document`, `replace_in_file_b64`, `session_broadcast`, `todo_create`, `todo_execute`, `understand_cwd`, `write_file_b64`
- [`_future/`](../../core/tools/_future/README.md), kept for later: `critic_validate`, `schema_validate`
- [`_template/`](../../core/tools/_template/README.md), the starting point for a new one
